name: mirage
text: Short answer: partly, and it's mostly done already, but I wouldn't rate stars directly on your own results. Today most bets are one star because the table only gives more than one star to bet types where the history proves a gain against Novig's closing price (CLV). Your taken bets, the engine's lines and the phone scans are already in that history. The 2026-10-24 study found that an edge over the outside books did not predict profit at Novig: most types lose and very few are proven. So one star is the honest result for most bets, not a bug in the scale. Using your own bets' profit as the scale (best 5 stars, worst 1) is risky. A few hundred bets in one type have wide error bars, so a type that happened to win would get 5 stars and then fall back to average. The star table was tested on later lines it hadn't seen for that reason. I think the useful version is a check, not a new rule. I can add a stars-versus-actual-results card to Stats: your ROI and CLV for every settled bet grouped by star, with the error bars. If higher stars really earn more on your bets, we keep the scale. If they don't, we change it. I'll add it to the task list and build it after the bet-speed and disappearing-bets work, unless you want it first.
